title: The Third Fork in the Road
next_chapter_hook: The light of the three-way ruins began to converge, the Tianji Record quivering violently as if something was about to break free—and Chen Ji, for the first time, felt the weight of fate.

text.content: The whisper of the remnant soul coiled around Chen Ji like a venomous snake, yet he smiled. That smile was平静得近乎残忍，像是在看一只自以为掌控全局的蝼蚁。他没有反驳，没有愤怒，只是静静地站在那里，任由那声音侵入耳膜。棋盘？棋子？呵。若他真是棋子，又怎会走到此处？天机录在识海中微微发烫，残页上的符文流转如水，映照出他眼底那抹深不见底的寒光。

"You are wrong." Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet it echoed through the empty ruins hall. "A chess piece does not question the chess player. A chess piece only moves according to the rules, until it is captured. And I—" He raised his hand, pointing at the three beams of light above. "I am seeking a fourth possibility." The moment his words fell, the entire ruins began to tremble. Those three motionless pillars of light suddenly blazed to life, cutting his figure into three parts, as if forcing him to make a choice.

dialogue.content: The first path leads to the core of Heaven's Will, to bear Heavenly Fate with my own body—the cost is eternal servitude as a puppet. The second path seals the Tianji Record, abandoning the power of prophecy—the cost is watching everyone I care about be crushed by fate. He paused, his eye sockets slightly reddening, yet forcibly suppressed that trace of vulnerability. "The third path... I don't know. But I remember Mother saying, Heaven never closes all doors."

text.content: When Chen Ji stepped into the third passage, a familiar yet heart-wrenching scent rushed toward him. It was neither spiritual energy nor killing intent, but—bloodline. The murals on both sides of the passage suddenly illuminated, depicting a breath-taking scene: a woman cradling an infant in her arms, behind her raging demonic flames, before her a bottomless abyss. She did not flee, but turned to face the pursuers behind her, her eyes burning with resolute flames.

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's footsteps abruptly stopped. His hands trembled uncontrollably, his fingertips almost touching the woman's face on the mural. In his Mental Sea, the Tianji Record churned violently, countless fragmented images flooding his mind—candlelight swaying in the night wind, a soft lullaby, a pair of warm yet helpless hands pushing him toward a safe corner... "Mother..." This name, never spoken before others, escaped his lips, his voice hoarse like shattered porcelain.

text.content: The mural slowly moved aside, revealing a secret stone chamber. Inside was only a statue of a woman cradling an infant, her features indistinct yet radiating a gentle glow. Carved on the statue's base were words: Chen Ji bent down to read, each character branding his heart like a searing iron: "My son, if you see this place, it means the Tianji Record has recognized you as its master. Mother cannot change fate, but I have left you a third path."

The statue's eyes suddenly glowed with soft light, and a phantom slowly emerged. Its features were unclear, yet it overlapped with the outline of his mother from Chen Ji's memories. She did not speak, only extending a hand as if wanting to stroke his cheek, yet could only pass through emptiness. Chen Ji stood there, tears finally overflowing, yet making no sound. He gritted his teeth, his shoulders heaving violently, as if undergoing a silent collapse.

Before the phantom completely faded, it left one final words, tender enough to break hearts: "Ji'er, do not fear sacrifice. True courage is not fearing death, but choosing to protect what you believe is worth guarding, even knowing you will die." The moment the words fell, the statue's base burst open, revealing a Jade Slip gleaming with golden light. Chen Ji trembled as he reached out, yet the instant he touched the Jade Slip, he felt a vast surge of information—his mother had sealed the third possibility with her life.

Information exploded within his Mental Sea, and Chen Ji witnessed a scene so tragic it stole one's breath: the Third Chess Player stood before the Eye of Heaven's Way, not yielding, not resisting, but choosing mutual destruction. Using herself as the conduit, she completely bound the Eye of Heaven's Way to her own fate—if Heaven's Way wished to exist, it must bear her suffering; if Heaven's Way were destroyed, she too would perish. This was玉石俱焚, yet also the most extreme form of resistance.

choice.prompt: Three paths, three fates. Chen Ji stood at fate's crossroads, feeling his mother's legacy boiling in his bloodline. Now, he must make a choice—

choices.description: Inherit the will of the Third Chess Player, choosing the path of mutual destruction with Heaven's Way.
choices.visible_reward: The possibility to completely break free from the shackles of fate
choices.risk_hint: This path requires sacrificing one's life, and the success rate is unknown

text.content: The moment Chen Ji grasped the Jade Slip, a warm spiritual energy flowed into his body, as if his mother was embracing him. "Very well, I accept." His voice was soft, yet resolute as an oath.

choices.description: Do not readily accept any path—use the Tianji Record to deduce a fourth possibility.
choices.visible_cost: Consume a large amount of Heavenly Fate
choices.visible_reward: Perhaps find a path that requires no sacrifice
choices.risk_hint: Each deduction consumes precious Heavenly Fate, which is the foundation of Chen Ji's survival

text.content: The Tianji Record flipped rapidly, Chen Ji tightly closing his eyes, veins bulging at his temples. He refused to accept any predetermined sacrifice, no matter how seemingly noble. Mother had paved the road for him, but its end should not be death.

choices.description: Seal Mother's legacy and return to choosing the relatively smaller cost among the first two paths.
choices.visible_reward: Maintain the status quo without taking greater risks
choices.risk_hint: This path means completely giving up the opportunity Mother traded with her life

text.content: Chen Ji's hand hovered over the Jade Slip, yet迟迟没有落下. His reason told him this was the most prudent choice; yet the warmth surging in his bloodline told him this was betrayal of his mother.

However, at this moment, an explosion echoed from outside the ruins. The three pillars of light began converging toward the center, a terrifying pressure sweeping from the passage's end. Chen Ji猛然抬头, for he sensed it—the aura of the Eye of Heaven's Way. It had detected the existence of the third path, spreading toward this place with irresistible force. Mo Xiansheng's voice rang in his Mental Sea, carrying unprecedented gravity: "It's here. Lad, you only have the time of one incense stick."

dialogue.content: Chen Ji closed his eyes and drew a deep breath. When he opened them again, the confusion had vanished, replaced by icy resolve. "Mo Xiansheng, help me stabilize the Tianji Record." He reached out, pressing the Jade Slip against the mark on his forehead. "Mother paved this road for me; I won't let her die for nothing. But I won't be foolish enough to go to my death now." His voice was low and dangerous. "I need time. I need to lay groundwork. I need to rescue Chen Nian first, and then—then we can destroy each other together."

text.content: The information from the Jade Slip was completely absorbed, and Chen Ji felt an unfamiliar yet familiar power flowing through his body. It was his mother's residual will, the final gift left by the Third Chess Player. He saw more—this was not merely a path of mutual destruction, but a complete plan, documenting how to lay an intricate web under the very eyes of the Eye of Heaven's Way, how to use every prophecy of the Tianji Record to weave a giant net, ultimately trapping the Eye of Heaven's Way forever.

But the cost was equally clear: the entire plan required at least ten years, during which he must constantly consume Heavenly Fate to maintain the arrangement; ten years during which he must watch those around him be harvested by fate one by one, yet cannot intervene—for any premature interference would expose the plan. And Chen Nian... that sister abducted by the Holy Sect was the key point of the entire plan. He must rescue her before the tenth year, otherwise everything would be meaningless.

choice.prompt: Ten years of laying groundwork, ten years of torment. Chen Ji now needed to decide how the first move should be made—

choices.text: First Establish the Groundwork, Then Rescue
choices.description: Follow Mother's left-behind plan steadily, develop forces covertly, wait for the right moment to rescue Chen Nian.
choices.visible_cost: Chen Nian may endure ten years of suffering
choices.risk_hint: Ten years brings too many variables; Chen Nian may not survive until then

dialogue.content: Chen Ji's fingers trembled slightly, yet quickly returned to calm. "Chen Nian, wait for your brother." He silently recited in his heart, a trace of painful tenderness flickering in his eyes.

choices.text: First Rescue Chen Nian, Then Establish the Groundwork
choices.description: Put rescuing as the top priority, even if it disrupts Mother's plan.
choices.visible_cost: The plan may need adjustment, reducing the success rate
choices.risk_hint: Premature action may expose one to the gaze of the Holy Sect and the Eye of Heaven's Way

dialogue.content: "Mother, I'm sorry." Chen Ji said softly, yet the resolve in his eyes did not diminish in the slightest. "I promised you I would protect what is worth protecting. Chen Nian is what I most want to protect."

text.content: The ruins' tremors grew increasingly violent, the pressure of the Eye of Heaven's Way was now within reach. Chen Ji knew he must leave. But in the instant he turned, he looked once more at the statue, his gaze tender as if returning to childhood. "Mother, I'm leaving." He said softly. "Wait for me to complete the plan, and then I will come keep you company." The statue glowed faintly, as if responding to his words. In that moment, Chen Ji felt a warmth wrapping around him, just like when he was held in his mother's arms as a child.

The convergence of the three pillars of light finally completed, a brilliant white light shooting skyward, illuminating the entire ruins as bright as day. The Tianji Record trembled violently, the runes on the fragmented pages疯狂流转, as if issuing a warning. Chen Ji's eyes snapped open—he sensed it, a power beyond his comprehension was gazing at him. That gaze was cold and vast, as if examining a ant attempting to shake a giant tree. The Eye of Heaven's Way had discovered him.

dialogue.content: A voice凭空响起, not the whisper of the remnant soul, but from a higher dimension, beyond soul, beyond perception: "Another ant, attempting to touch fate that does not belong to you." That voice carried no emotion, yet was more suffocating than any pressure. "You think your mother left you a path? No, that is merely the entrance to another prison." Chen Ji stood in place, facing an existence beyond comprehension, yet the corner of his mouth lifted in a cold smile.

text.content: "Is that so?" Chen Ji's voice was soft, yet clearly entered that omnipresent consciousness. "Then let me see what this prison holds—blades or fire." He turned, striding toward the exit, his back决绝而孤独. That transcendental gaze watched him leave, yet did not stop him—not unable, but disdainful. In the eyes of the Eye of Heaven's Way, Chen Ji was merely another chess piece that would inevitably fall onto the board. And this was precisely what Chen Ji wanted it to believe.

The moment Chen Ji stepped out of the ruins, the three pillars of light simultaneously dissipated, leaving only a sky平静得近乎诡异. He stood at the cliff's edge,山风吹乱发丝, his eye sockets slightly red yet his gaze resolute. Behind him lay his mother's legacy; before him stretched the ten-year road of laying groundwork. The Tianji Record slowly rotated in his Mental Sea, the runes on the fragmented pages glowing brighter than before—a blessing from his mother, and the first web of chess he was weaving for his sister and all he cared about. Ten years—he had ten years to turn the entire world into his chessboard. And now, the game had just begun.
